persist.notice: Reported numbers arrive late, miss cases that were never tested or reported, and use definitions that differ between sources and countries.
footer.positioning: Understanding Outbreaks aggregates and explains official public reports.
footer.licenseData: Data: each source keeps its own license (shown in every trace panel and export)
footer.privacy: No tracking, no analytics, no cookies, no third-party requests
footer.attribution: Boundaries: Natural Earth. Places: GeoNames. Population: World Bank. Basemap, where shown: © OpenStreetMap contributors, Protomaps.
state.error: This data could not be loaded.
origin.source-reported.explain: Published by the source named below. This site shows it without changing the value.
origin.site-derived.explain: Computed by this project from the sources named below. The method and its inputs are listed here.
origin.user-supplied.explain: Supplied by you in this browser. It was not uploaded and is not part of the official data.
origin.simulated.explain: Output of the educational simulation sandbox. It is illustrative, not fitted to data, and not a forecast.
origin.test-data.explain: Test fixture. Not real. It must never appear on the published site.
trace.title: Trace this
trace.archivedCopy: Archived copy of the raw file
trace.notRedistributed: Raw file not redistributed (license); its hash and link are recorded
trace.transformations: What was done to the data
trace.footer: Every number on this site can be followed back to the publication it came from. If a link is broken, use the archived copy.
status.reported.explain: An official source published a notice about this event recently. The notice does not state whether it is ongoing.
status.ongoing.explain: The latest official notice describes the event as ongoing.
status.declared_over.explain: The latest official notice says the outbreak was declared over.
status.no_recent_update.explain: No official notice has been published for more than 90 days. This is a recency indicator, not a judgment that the outbreak ended.
chart.incompleteTip: Recent periods are usually revised upward as late reports arrive. A drop here is not a real decline.
chart.incompleteNote: The most recent periods are probably still being reported. They are shaded and left out of trends and percentage changes.
chart.whyLow: Why do recent weeks look low?
chart.heatScale: darker = more, up to {max}; hatched = no data
transform.perCapita.explain: Divided by population and multiplied by 100,000, so places of different size can be compared.
transform.cumulative.explain: Added up over time into a running total. Missing periods add nothing.
transform.rolling.explain: Averaged over a trailing window to smooth week-to-week noise. A window with a missing period is left blank.
transform.rebase.explain: Each series shown as a percentage of its own highest value.
transform.align.explain: Each series starts at its first reported case, so outbreaks that began at different times can be compared.
transform.log.explain: Drawn on a logarithmic scale (display only; values are unchanged).
transform.excludeIncomplete.explain: Recent periods marked likely incomplete were removed.
table.label: Data table
table.truncated: Showing the {n} most recent of {total} rows. Download the data for all rows.
warn.mixedDefinitions: This view combines different case definitions ({defs}). Their numbers are not directly comparable.
warn.mixedSources: This view combines different sources ({sources}). They may count differently.
warn.mixedSeries: Definitions differ between countries and years in this series (the broadest available definition is used for each). Do not use it to rank countries.
warn.crossDisease: Counts for different diseases come from different surveillance systems and case definitions. Do not compare their size directly.
warn.incompleteIncluded: This result includes periods marked likely incomplete.
embed.title: Embed this view
embed.intro: Paste this code into a page. The embed is a minimal, accessible version of this view with its source and trace link kept.
embed.pinned: The embed is pinned to snapshot {snapshot}, so it will keep showing exactly these numbers. Remove the snapshot parameter to always show the latest data.
embed.privacy: Embeds load only this site’s own files, set no cookies and make no third-party requests.
api.intro: These static files hold the values behind this view. They are plain JSON and can be fetched directly.
code.intro: This code reproduces the exact view, including filters and transforms, from the published revision history at snapshot {snapshot}.
overview.title: Infectious disease activity, as officially reported
overview.lead: A sourced view of what official public reports say about infectious disease activity around the world. Every number links back to where it came from.
overview.means.rate: Darker areas reported more cases per 100,000 people in the period {window}. Hatched areas have no report for that period, which is not the same as zero cases.
overview.means.pct: Darker areas had a larger share of tested samples positive for influenza in the period {window}. Hatched areas have no report for that period.
overview.means.caveat: Countries test and report very differently, so a high value can reflect better detection as well as more disease.
overview.activeSub: From official event notices, in a documented list order. The order is not a rating of how serious an event is.
overview.noActive: No recent event notices match these filters.
overview.trendsSub: Totals across the countries that reported to each source. The dashed end of each line covers periods that are likely incomplete.
flags.title: Automated signal flags
flags.neutral: Informational labels from a simple statistical check. They are not alerts or judgments.
flags.caveat: Flags can be triggered by reporting changes, batches of late reports or testing drives, and many real changes are not flagged.
flags.text: Reported counts are unusually high compared with this place’s recent baseline (method {method}).
flags.more: {n, plural, one {# recent period} other {# recent periods}} flagged.
flags.count: {n, plural, one {# period in the past year} other {# periods in the past year}}.
flags.detail: Reported {value}; baseline mean {mean}; threshold {threshold}; baseline window {from} to {to}.
flags.none: No flags in the recent period.
flags.learn: Why a flag is not a prediction
flagstatus.suppressed-possible-batch-rep: Not flagged: follows a gap, possible batch reporting
flagstatus.suppressed-seasonal-baseline-: Not flagged: too little history for the seasonal check
flagstatus.suppressed-within-seasonal-ra: Not flagged: within the usual seasonal range
map.aria: Map: {title}. A table version is available with the “View as table” button.
map.cluster: {n, plural, one {# reported location} other {# reported locations}}
map.failed: The map could not be loaded. Use the table view instead.
map.drawHint: Click the map to add corners ({n} so far).
map.metric.rate.W: Cases per 100,000 people, most recent {n} complete weeks
map.metric.rate.M: Cases per 100,000 people, most recent complete month
map.metric.rate.Y: Cases per 100,000 people, most recent complete year
map.metric.percentPositive: Percent of tested samples positive, most recent {n} complete weeks
map.metric.ratePeriod: Cases per 100,000 people in the period
map.metric.pctPeriod: Percent of tested samples positive in the period
map.attr.boundaries: Boundaries: Natural Earth (public domain). Boundaries are approximate and imply no position on any territory.
map.attr.gazetteer: Place positions: GeoNames (CC BY 4.0), derived by this site.
mappage.title: Map
mappage.lead: Move through time, switch layers, and see where official event notices place reported outbreaks. The address bar always holds a link to exactly this view.
mappage.means.disease: Colours use one fixed scale for every period, so you can compare periods fairly. Hatched areas have no report for the selected period.
mappage.means.density: Population density is shown for context only. It is a country average and hides large differences within countries.
mappage.means.points: Points show where official notices place an event. A point at country precision sits at the middle of the country and is not the location of cases.
place.noSeries: No time series is available for {name} from the current sources. Event notices, if any, are listed below.
place.means.cases: Each point is the number officially reported for {name} in that period. Reports arrive late and many infections are never tested or reported, so the true number is higher.
place.means.detections: Each point is the number of laboratory samples that tested positive in {name}. It reflects how much testing was done as well as how much virus was circulating.
place.neighboursMeans: Shown per 100,000 people so countries of different size can be compared. Differences also reflect how much each country tests and reports.
place.subnationalNone: None of the current open sources publishes sub-national time series for this country, so no drill-down is shown rather than a guess.
place.noEvents: No official event notices are on record for this country in the period covered.
lag.line: Reporting lag: {n, plural, =0 {none assumed} one {# period} other {# periods}} ({basis}).
lag.basis.configured-default: configured default until enough snapshots exist
reconcile.title: Sources side by side: {name}
reconcile.agree: More than one source reports this series. Their values agree within the tolerance in the methodology. Both are shown; neither is merged.
reconcile.disagree: More than one source reports this series, and they disagree in {n, plural, one {# period} other {# periods}}. Both are shown; this site does not pick a winner.
revisions.title: How values were revised
revisions.none: No value for this place has been revised since it first appeared ({n, plural, one {# snapshot} other {# snapshots}} so far).
pin.banner: You are viewing data as it was published on {date} (snapshot {id}).
pin.vintage: Vintage reflects what this site retrieved and published, not necessarily when a source first released a number.
pin.unknown: Snapshot {id} is not known. Showing the latest data.
pin.count: {n, plural, one {# snapshot so far.} other {# snapshots so far.}}
diseases.title: Diseases
diseases.lead: Diseases with a time series show reported counts over time. Diseases marked “event reports only” are covered through official outbreak notices.
diseases.events: {n, plural, =0 {no event notices} one {# event} other {# events}}
diseases.otherNote: Names from official notices that are not yet in the disease mapping. They are never guessed.
disease.leadTs: Reported {name} counts over time, with the official event notices that mention it.
disease.leadEvents: There is no reliable open time series for {name}. It is covered through official event notices.
disease.globalMeans: This adds up what countries reported to the source. The number of countries reporting changes over time, so part of any rise or fall is a change in who reported.
disease.topCaveat: countries that test and report more appear higher
disease.noEvents: No official event notices are on record for this disease in the period covered.
disease.seriesSub: Each series keeps its own source, case definition and surveillance system. They are never silently combined.
disease.reconcile: Sources overlap in {overlaps} country-periods and disagree in {n}.
disease.idsNote: Identifiers are filled only where the mapping is clear, and are flagged for human review.
outbreaks.title: Reported outbreaks
outbreaks.lead: Every event in official notices from the sources this site reads, grouped into one timeline per event.
outbreaks.includeOld: Include events with no recent update
outbreaks.rankNote: The list order uses a documented formula based on recency, reported counts, number of countries and source type. It is not a severity rating.
rank.title: List order
rank.formula: score = Σ weight × component (method active_rank v1). Weights:
event.summaryNote: Written by this site from the notices’ titles, dates and quoted phrases. It is not the source’s own wording.
event.sum.intro: {source} published {n, plural, one {# notice} other {# notices}} about {disease} concerning {places}, first on {first} and most recently on {last}.
event.sum.noCounts: The notices do not state a case count that could be read automatically.
outbreak.daysAgo: {n, plural, =0 {today} one {# day ago} other {# days ago}}
outbreak.countsNote: Counts are read automatically from the notice text and shown with the exact phrase. Always check the original notice.
outbreak.noLocation: The notices do not name a single country, so no location is shown.
outbreak.precisionNote: Locations are derived by this site from place names in the notice. Precision is shown for each. A country-level point is the middle of the country, not where cases occurred.
changes.title: What changed this week
changes.lead: A factual list of what is new in the official reports between {from} and {to}.
changes.moversCaveat: Changes compare the two most recent periods that are not marked likely incomplete. They can still be revised, and may reflect reporting rather than disease.
changelog.title: Changelog and corrections
changelog.lead: Methodology changes, pipeline fixes, mapping changes and corrected errors, with dates.
quality.title: Data quality
quality.lead: How fresh, complete and stable each source is. This table is produced by the pipeline on every run, not written by hand.
quality.snapshots: {n, plural, one {Based on # snapshot.} other {Based on # snapshots.}}
quality.daysOld: ended {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago
quality.lagPeriods: {n, plural, =0 {none assumed} one {# period} other {# periods}}
sources.lead: The source registry. Every chart, map, table and export on this site refers to one or more of these entries.
cite.lead: How to cite this site, a specific snapshot, and the original sources.
cite.noDoi: No DOI has been minted yet. A maintainer must complete the release steps in the README first. Until then, cite the snapshot id above.
researchers.lead: Bulk downloads, a static JSON API, data dictionaries and in-browser analysis tools. Everything carries its sources.
researchers.explorer: Filter diseases, places, dates, definitions, sources and data vintage, then preview and export.
researchers.workbench: SQL console, notebooks, pivot tables, chart builder, snapshot diff and your own data overlay. Runs in your browser.
researchers.cite: Citation text, machine-readable metadata and the release process.
researchers.bulkNote: Latest snapshot: {snapshot}. Parquet files are sorted by place and date so they can be queried over HTTP without a full download.
researchers.flags: Signal flags (with method version and parameters)
researchers.apiNote: All endpoints are plain files under the data path. Record ids have the form series_id@period; the lineage file for a disease and country lists the raw record reference and raw file for every value.
researchers.snapshots: {n, plural, one {# immutable snapshot is listed in} other {# immutable snapshots are listed in}}
endpoint.timeseries: Time series for one disease and country
endpoint.lineage: Lineage for every value of one disease and country
endpoint.revisions: Revision history for one disease and country
endpoint.event: One event with its notices and history
endpoint.overview: Map and trend summary for one disease
explorer.title: Data Explorer
explorer.lead: Choose what to look at, check it in the preview, and download it with its sources attached.
explorer.means: By default this shows each disease’s default series per 100,000 people, with likely-incomplete periods hidden. Change the options above the chart to see raw counts or other series.
explorer.bulk: Full datasets, data dictionary and API:
explorer.vintageHint: Switch to Analyst mode to choose an earlier “data as of” snapshot.
explorer.eventsNote: Exports include each derived location with its precision and the geocoding method.
explorer.revCount: {n, plural, =0 {No values have changed since they first appeared} one {# recorded change} other {# recorded changes}} across {snapshots, plural, one {# snapshot} other {# snapshots}}.
firstuse.compare.title: Before you compare
firstuse.compare.body: Countries and sources count differently. Compare rates per 100,000 rather than raw counts, keep to one case definition, and leave out the most recent periods, which are still being reported.
context.title: Related official and scientific resources
context.note: These links leave this site. Nothing is loaded from them unless you click.
watch.title: Watchlists
watch.lead: Keep a short list of the places, diseases and events you follow. It lives in your browser and in the link you share; there are no accounts.
watch.empty: Your watchlist is empty. Use “Add to watchlist” on a country, disease or outbreak page.
watch.badFile: That file is not a watchlist exported from this site.
watch.shared: You are viewing a shared watchlist.
watch.privacy: Nothing is sent to a server. If your browser blocks storage, the shareable link and the exported file still work.
workbench.title: Analysis workbench
glossary.lead: Plain-language meanings of the terms used on this site.
guide.lead: Short, practical guidance for writing about outbreak numbers accurately.
guide.attributionText: Source: [name of the original source, e.g. World Health Organization], via {site} ({url}), data as of [date]. Reported cases are an undercount and recent periods are incomplete.
guide.evidence: Claims in this guide that rest on outside evidence cite their sources in the text. Wording about health is flagged for human review in every translation.
methodology.lead: How the numbers on this site are collected, checked, computed and labelled.
methodology.paramsNote: Read live from the published data, so this always matches what the pipeline used.
